status_history.reason: Extracted from CASE-007 production design; not yet validated against current HyperFrames rendering, three-mode compositing, or cross-aspect-ratio frame inspection.

title: Neon Cyber Overlay
summary: A transparent technical information layer designed to sit over talking-head footage. Functional coding over atmospheric immersion — API blocks, status colors, registration marks, and semi-transparent dark cards with hard-alpha delivery.
avoid_for: segments requiring a full-screen immersive background

canvas.tone: transparent cyber-functional — white body text over a clear base, with cyan, pink, and purple as functional coding colors on semi-transparent dark cards and thin luminous registration marks.
canvas.background_policy: The canvas is transparent by default so the overlay composites over talking-head footage. Opaque elements are confined to semi-transparent dark cards and functional HUD lines; the background itself must not block the host.

palette.strategy: One white body role plus three functional signal roles (cyan, pink, purple). Each signal color encodes a distinct semantic category; all three must not flood the frame simultaneously.

roles.semantic: primary readable text on transparent ground
roles.value_policy: white with sufficient contrast against the semi-transparent dark card backing

roles.semantic: API endpoints, method names, code identifiers
roles.value_policy: cyan accent, used sparingly as a functional label color

roles.semantic: success states, confirmed results, passing checks
roles.value_policy: green-cyan or bright green accent, applied only when a real success condition is shown
pink or purple accent, applied only when a real constraint or error is shown

roles.purpose: single-message headline or API route label
roles.style_relation: largest weight on screen, white, short and punchy

roles.purpose: code blocks, terminal output, technical identifiers
roles.style_relation: monospace, smaller than display, cyan or white depending on semantic role
smallest, thinnest, mono, low opacity white or functional color

typography.local_fallback_policy: Select installed monospace and sans-serif fonts by role; verify actual rendered glyph coverage for code points and CJK if mixed-language content is present.

visual_system.whitespace_policy: Left-align or two-column split; reserve empty transparent space around the hero block so the host remains visible behind the overlay.

focus_policy.rule: One code block, API label, or status message owns each shot; registration marks and HUD lines remain subordinate.

purposes: present an API endpoint or code snippet
scene_grammar.composition: Left-aligned code block on a semi-transparent dark card with a cyan functional label above or beside it. Registration marks frame the block corners.
required_semantics: a real API endpoint, method, or code identifier
a functional category that justifies the color choice
forbidden_uses: fake code that serves only as decoration
code rain or scrolling terminal without readable content

scene_grammar.composition: A single status message with its semantic color (green for success, pink/purple for constraint) on a dark card, accompanied by a thin luminous indicator line.
required_semantics: a real success or constraint condition from the content
a distinct result state the narration names
forbidden_uses: decorative status badges without a real condition
mixing success and constraint colors in the same shot without clear hierarchy

scene_grammar.composition: Two-column split with left and right dark cards. Each column carries its own functional label color; the comparison direction is reinforced by a thin luminous divider.
required_semantics: two real, distinct technical states or options
a comparison axis the narration names
forbidden_uses: three or more columns that fragment focus

purposes: illustrate a data flow or pipeline
scene_grammar.composition: Left-aligned or centered structural diagram with labeled nodes connected by thin luminous lines. Each node uses its semantic color; the flow direction is readable at a glance.
required_semantics: a real system structure or data flow
nodes that correspond to named entities in the narration
forbidden_uses: generic three-box arrow diagrams without real entities
overly complex graphs that cannot be read within the shot duration

entries.semantic_trigger: The narration introduces an API, endpoint, or code concept.
entries.action: The code block card scales in rapidly with a brief blur-crossfade that resolves to sharp focus as the block lands.
entries.result_state: The code block is fully readable with its functional label visible; registration marks are steady.
entries.hold_policy: Hold the readable result state for the duration of the code explanation; do not animate out until the next semantic beat.

entries.semantic_trigger: The narration names a success, error, or constraint outcome.
entries.action: A thin luminous indicator line draws on horizontally, then the status text fades in beside it with the semantic color.
entries.result_state: The status line and text are steady; the semantic color is the only accent in the frame.
entries.hold_policy: Reserve a content-dependent result hold; the status must remain readable until the next beat or cut.

entries.semantic_trigger: Continuous during any shot that uses registration marks or HUD lines.
entries.action: Registration marks and thin HUD lines breathe subtly — a slow opacity pulse or sub-pixel drift that maintains spatial reference without drawing focus.
entries.result_state: The marks remain visible but subordinate; the primary content block holds focus.
entries.hold_policy: Continuous ambient motion that does not compete with the active semantic action. Must be seek-safe and deterministic.

transitions.semantic_trigger: Transition between two technical shots when the pacing accelerates.
transitions.action: Apply a brief directional blur that matches the incoming motion vector, then resolve to sharp focus as the next shot lands.
transitions.result_state: The next shot is sharp and readable; the blur is fully resolved within the first frames of the new shot.
transitions.hold_policy: No hold — the transition is the action. The result state is the beginning of the next semantic entry.

global_rules: Derive all motion from deterministic local time; every entry must be seek-safe.
Fast entries and blur transitions must not overshoot or leave residual motion blur in the hold state.
Ambient breathing must never compete with the active semantic entry; reduce ambient intensity when a primary action is running.
Simplify the choreography when the fixed SRT window cannot contain the full entry-plus-hold sequence.

modes.usage: Default delivery mode. Opaque semantic objects (code blocks, status text, dark cards, registration marks) are isolated on a transparent background with crisp alpha edges. No soft glow, blur, or semi-transparent fringing in the alpha channel.
constraints: Move all soft glow and luminous bloom to a separate black-background-light layer.
Verify alpha edges are hard and free of premultiplication artifacts.
Semi-transparent dark cards must use straight alpha, not additive blend.

modes.usage: Optional companion layer for soft glow, luminous bloom, and thin-line light effects that cannot be expressed as hard-alpha. Rendered as black-background MP4 for screen or add blend in post.
constraints: Only the glow and luminous elements appear on black; never include opaque cards or text in this layer.
Verify black level is true zero so the blend mode works correctly in the editing timeline.
This mode is optional — a shot with no glow effects does not need a black-background-light companion.

modes.usage: Fallback when the overlay must stand alone without host footage (e.g., standalone preview or sections with no talking-head). Uses a near-black opaque background instead of transparency.
constraints: Do not use fullscreen mode when the shot is intended as an overlay over host footage.
The opaque background must match the dark card tone so the visual system remains coherent.

hard_rules: Choose the scene grammar from the sentence meaning before selecting a color or component.
Keep the SRT timeline fixed; motion must fit within the given window.
Each shot has exactly one primary code block, status message, or diagram node as the hero focus.
Cyan, pink, and purple are functional coding colors only; do not use all three as大面积 decoration in one shot.
Never fabricate code, API output, or status results to fill a layout.
do: Make code blocks and status messages readable without subtitles.
Use the host's talking-head footage as the ground layer; let the overlay supplement, not replace.
Apply only one functional color dominance per shot.
Leave transparent space around the hero block so the host remains visible.
dont: Copy the OculOS brand signature, logo, or product name.
Use WebM Alpha as a production delivery format.
Flood the frame with all three functional colors simultaneously.
Use code rain, scrolling terminal, or AI orbs as filler.
Treat the overlay as a full-screen immersive background.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Shift the functional color balance based on whether the content is API-heavy, evenly mixed, or focused on errors and limits.
constraints: Never use all three colors at equal dominance in one shot.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Adjust dark card transparency to balance code readability against host visibility.
constraints: Never drop below 0.5 — the card must remain readable.
Never exceed 0.9 — the host must remain visible behind the card.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Control whether code blocks, labels, or a mix dominate the frame based on content density.
constraints: A label-forward shot must still contain a real technical identifier.
A code-forward shot must still have a readable functional label.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Scale luminous glow intensity from none to moderate; higher values push more content into the black-background-light companion layer.
constraints: At 0, no black-background-light companion is needed.
Glow must never bleed into the hard-alpha channel.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Control how much of the frame the overlay occupies — a contained block, a half-frame split, or edge-anchored HUD elements.
constraints: Edge mode must still leave the host's face unobstructed.
Split mode must not exceed 50 percent frame coverage.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Match entry speed to the narration pace — fast for dense technical walkthroughs, measured for explanations with pauses.
constraints: Fast entries must still resolve to a readable hold state.
Measured entries must not feel sluggish against spoken content.

signature_motifs.description: Transparent ground, white body text, and three functional coding colors (cyan for API/identifiers, green for success, pink/purple for constraints) applied to semi-transparent dark cards with registration marks.

exhausted_motifs.reason: Scrolling terminal or code-rain animations replace actual technical content with a generic cyber symbol. Only show real, readable code when the code itself is evidence.

The three functional colors are already the signature motif of this template. When borrowing into another template, each color use must be justified by a real semantic category in the content — never use all three as decoration.

conflicts_with.reason: Warm red-gold serif presentation competes with cool cyan-pink-purple transparent cyber functional coding. The palettes, type roles, and spatial hierarchies are incompatible.
conflicts_with.resolution: If overlay is required over red-gold content, reduce to a single warm-white-plus-gold monochrome adaptation; do not mix the cyber tricolor with the forbidden-red palette.

conflicts_with.reason: Surge is a full-screen brand manifesto with four-color gradients and metal big-type punch-ins. Cyber is a transparent functional information layer. Their background policies and motion energies collide.
conflicts_with.resolution: Borrow at most the off-center composition or a short punchy label from Surge; do not bring the four-color ribbon gradient, metal big-type, or full-screen dark background into the transparent overlay.

borrowable_patterns.description: A portable status-indicator pattern: thin line draws on, then text fades in with a semantic color. Usable by any template that needs to show success or constraint states.
conditions: The content names a real success or constraint.
The borrowing template restyles the line weight and color to its own palette.

borrowable_patterns.description: A directional blur transition that matches incoming motion and resolves to sharp focus. Portable across technical templates.
conditions: The transition connects two shots with clear motion direction.
The borrowing template verifies seek-safe behavior with its own timeline.

restrictions: Do not distribute source media, private copy, local paths, or OculOS brand identifiers.

forbidden_materials: private source media and business copy
OculOS brand name, logo, product UI, and fixed copy
source code from the original CASE-007 project

stale_rules.original_claim: CASE-007 used WebM Alpha as the default transparent overlay delivery format.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: Current product contract mandates hard-alpha default as ProRes 4444 MOV; glow and particles default to black-background MP4. WebM Alpha is experimental only and must not be used as a production delivery format.
